syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 1
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'diligent':
explanation: Diligent means showing persistent care, effort, and hard work.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 2
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'candid':
explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward; frank.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 3
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'abundant':
explanation: Abundant means existing or available in large quantities; overflowing.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 4
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'hostile':
explanation: Hostile means showing or feeling active opposition or unfriendliness.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 5
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'lucid':
explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly; easy to comprehend.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 6
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'frugal':
explanation: Frugal means sparing or economical with regard to money or food.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 7
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'pensive':
explanation: Pensive means engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 8
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'lethal':
explanation: Lethal means sufficient to cause death; fatal.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 9
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'meticulous':
explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 10
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'obstinate':
explanation: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 11
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'indolent':
explanation: Indolent means wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 12
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'audacious':
explanation: Audacious means showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 13
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'ambiguous':
options: Having more than one possible meaning
explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 14
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'benevolent':
explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly; charitable.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 15
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'covert':
explanation: Covert means not openly acknowledged or displayed; secret.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 16
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'prolific':
explanation: Prolific means producing much fruit or foliage or many works.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 17
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'tedious':
explanation: Tedious means too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 18
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'resilient':
options: Able to recover quickly from difficulties
explanation: Resilient means able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 19
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'vivid':
explanation: Vivid means producing powerful feelings or strong, clear images in the mind.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Vocabulary Item 20
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'wary':
explanation: Wary means feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 21
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'fragile':
explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken; its true antonym is 'sturdy' or 'robust'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 22
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'arrogant':
explanation: Arrogant means having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance; its opposite is humble.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 23
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'scarce':
explanation: Scarce means insufficient for the demand; plentiful is the exact opposite.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 24
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'lenient':
explanation: Lenient means more merciful or tolerant than expected; strict is the antonym.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 25
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'transparent':
explanation: Transparent means permitting light to pass through clearly; opaque blocks light completely.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 26
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'optimistic':
explanation: Optimistic means expecting good outcomes; pessimistic expects the worst.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 27
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'voluntary':
explanation: Voluntary means done of one's own free will; compulsory means mandatory.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 28
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'hostile':
explanation: Hostile means unfriendly; amicable means characterized by friendliness.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 29
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'obscure':
explanation: Obscure means not known or important; famous means widely known.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 30
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'fictitious':
explanation: Fictitious means created from the imagination; authentic means genuine and true.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 31
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'permanent':
explanation: Permanent means lasting indefinitely; temporary means lasting for a limited time.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 32
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'rigid':
explanation: Rigid means unable to bend; flexible means capable of bending easily.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 33
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'expand':
explanation: Expand means to become larger; contract means to decrease in size.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 34
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'guilty':
explanation: Guilty means responsible for a specified wrongdoing; innocent means free from guilt.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 35
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'hazard':
explanation: Hazard means a potential source of danger; safety is freedom from danger.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 36
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'harmony':
explanation: Harmony means agreement and concord; discord is disagreement between people.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 37
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'reckless':
explanation: Reckless means without thinking of consequences; prudent shows foresight and care.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 38
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'trivial':
explanation: Trivial means of little value or importance; crucial means decisive or critical.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 39
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'generous':
explanation: Generous means showing readiness to give; miserly means hoarding and refusing to give.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Antonyms Item 40
stem: Select the word opposite in meaning to 'vague':
explanation: Vague means uncertain or indefinite; precise means exact and accurate.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 41
stem: Identify the correct preposition: 'Ama is interested _____ pursuing civil engineering.'
explanation: The adjective 'interested' collocates specifically with the preposition 'in'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 42
stem: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the headmaster nor the teachers _____ at the meeting.'
explanation: In 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('teachers', plural: were).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 43
stem: Choose the correct verb: 'Every one of the applicants _____ qualified for the scholarship.'
explanation: 'Every one' is grammatically singular and takes a singular verb: 'is'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 44
stem: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The committee submitted the annual financial report.'
options: The annual financial report was submitted by the committee.
explanation: Past simple active 'submitted' becomes 'was submitted' in standard passive voice.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Punctuation Item 45
stem: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
options: Although it was raining heavily, the students walked to school.
Although it was raining heavily the students walked to school.
Although, it was raining heavily the students walked to school.
Although it was raining heavily; the students walked.
explanation: A subordinate introductory clause must be separated from the main clause by a comma.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 46
stem: Complete the sentence: 'She had hardly entered the hall _____ the lecture began.'
explanation: 'Hardly' and 'scarcely' pair correlatively with 'when' (not 'than').

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 47
stem: Complete the sentence: 'No sooner had the bell rung _____ the children rushed out.'
explanation: 'No sooner' pairs strictly with 'than' in inverted introductory time structures.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 48
stem: Choose the correct tag: 'You will submit your project tomorrow, _____?'
explanation: A positive statement with auxiliary 'will' takes a negative tag: 'won't you?'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 49
stem: Choose the correct tag: 'The candidates have not completed the test, _____?'
explanation: A negative statement with 'have not' takes a positive tag: 'have they?'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 50
stem: Choose the correct conditional form: 'If I had seen Kwame, I _____ him the good news.'
explanation: Third conditional uses 'if + had + past participle' followed by 'would have + past participle'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 51
stem: Choose the correct form: 'The luggage _____ too heavy for the boy to carry.'
explanation: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun in English and strictly takes a singular verb.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 52
stem: Choose the correct form: 'The police _____ investigating the cause of the fire outbreak.'
explanation: 'Police' is a plural collective noun requiring a plural verb: 'are'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 53
stem: Choose the correct word: 'Between you and _____, the test was rather difficult.'
explanation: 'Between' is a preposition requiring an objective case pronoun: 'between you and me'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 54
stem: Choose the correct option: 'Kwame prefers reading novels _____ watching movies.'
explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' when comparing two activities.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 55
stem: Choose the correct pronoun: 'One must do _____ best in every examination.'
explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'one' takes the possessive form 'one's'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 56
stem: Choose the correct option: 'The news broadcast by GBC yesterday _____ encouraging.'
explanation: 'News' is grammatically singular and takes the singular verb 'was'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 57
stem: Choose the correct preposition: 'The student was accused _____ cheating in the mock examination.'
explanation: The verb 'accuse' is followed by the preposition 'of'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 58
stem: Choose the correct preposition: 'The headmistress congratulated the debate team _____ their victory.'
explanation: One congratulates someone 'on' an achievement or milestone.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 59
stem: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The lady _____ car broke down was assisted by the mechanics.'
explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun referring to ownership.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Grammar Item 60
stem: Choose the correct word: 'Neither of the two candidates _____ selected for the interview.'
explanation: 'Neither of the two' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'was'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 61
stem: What does the idiom 'to beat about the bush' mean?
options: To avoid talking directly about what is important
To clear a path in the forest
explanation: To beat about the bush means to discuss a matter without coming directly to the point.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 62
stem: What does the idiom 'to see eye to eye' mean?
options: To look directly at someone's face
explanation: 'To see eye to eye' means to be in complete agreement with another person.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 63
stem: What does the idiom 'a white elephant' mean?
options: A possession that is useless and expensive to maintain
explanation: A white elephant is a possession that is useless or troublesome, especially one that is expensive to maintain.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 64
stem: What does the idiom 'to cry over spilt milk' mean?
options: To worry about past mistakes that cannot be undone
explanation: It means wasting time worrying or regretting something that has already happened and cannot be altered.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 65
stem: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
options: To describe exactly what is causing a situation
explanation: To hit the nail on the head means to find the exact answer or identify the core truth.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 66
stem: What does the idiom 'to turn a blind eye' mean?
options: To knowingly pretend not to notice something wrong
explanation: Turning a blind eye means deliberately ignoring or pretending not to notice bad behavior.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 67
stem: What does the idiom 'to bark up the wrong tree' mean?
options: To pursue a mistaken line of thought or action
explanation: It means having a completely false idea or pursuing a wrong course of inquiry.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 68
stem: What does the idiom 'burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To study or work late into the night
explanation: Burning the midnight oil refers to staying up late studying or working diligently.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 69
stem: What does the idiom 'under the weather' mean?
explanation: Being 'under the weather' is an idiom meaning slightly unwell or depressed.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 70
stem: What does the idiom 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: A good thing that seemed bad at first
A costume worn at a festival
explanation: A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that eventually has good results.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 71
stem: What does the idiom 'bite the bullet' mean?
options: To endure an unavoidable painful experience courageously
explanation: To bite the bullet means to face a difficult situation with courage and fortitude.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 72
stem: What does the idiom 'spill the beans' mean?
explanation: Spilling the beans means unintentionally or prematurely revealing a secret.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 73
stem: What does the idiom 'cost an arm and a leg' mean?
explanation: 'Costing an arm and a leg' denotes an excessively high price.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 74
stem: What does the idiom 'cut corners' mean?
options: To do something badly or cheaply to save time or money
explanation: Cutting corners means undertaking a task without due thoroughness to economize time or funds.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 75
stem: What does the idiom 'piece of cake' mean?
options: Something that is very easy to accomplish
explanation: 'A piece of cake' characterizes a task that is exceptionally easy and straightforward.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 76
stem: What does the idiom 'at the eleventh hour' mean?
explanation: The eleventh hour denotes the latest possible moment before a deadline.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 77
stem: What does the idiom 'throw in the towel' mean?
options: To dry one's face after sports
explanation: Originating in boxing, throwing in the towel signifies admitting defeat and quitting.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 78
stem: What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
options: To make people feel more relaxed in a social setting
To crush ice blocks in a freezer
To go fishing in cold regions
explanation: Breaking the ice means initiating conversation to relieve social awkwardness.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 79
stem: What does the idiom 'let the cat out of the bag' mean?
options: To reveal a secret by mistake
explanation: It means allowing a secret to become known, often carelessly or unexpectedly.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Idioms Item 80
stem: What does the idiom 'take with a pinch of salt' mean?
options: To view a statement with skepticism
explanation: To take something with a pinch of salt means not completely believing what one is told.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Spelling Item 81
stem: Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning to provide lodging or room for:
explanation: 'Accommodate' is correctly spelled with double 'c' and double 'm'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Spelling Item 82
stem: Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning an incident or event that happens:
explanation: 'Occurrence' requires double 'c', double 'r', and the suffix '-ence'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Spelling Item 83
stem: Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning a special right, advantage, or immunity:
explanation: 'Privilege' has no 'd' in its spelling.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Spelling Item 84
stem: Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning a feeling of self-conscious distress or shame:
explanation: 'Embarrassment' is spelled with double 'r' and double 's'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Spelling Item 85
stem: Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning the process of preserving a condition or situation:
explanation: The noun form derived from 'maintain' is spelled 'maintenance'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 86
stem: What figure of speech gives human attributes to non-human entities?
explanation: Personification attributes human qualities, emotions, or behaviors to animals or objects.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 87
stem: Identify the literary device in: 'The camel is the ship of the desert.'
explanation: A metaphor makes a direct comparison without using 'like' or 'as'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 88
stem: Identify the figure of speech in: 'Her tears flowed like an endless river.'
explanation: A simile uses comparison words such as 'like' or 'as'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 89
stem: Identify the figure of speech in: 'The thunder roared angrily across the valley.'
explanation: Attributing anger to thunder is a classic example of personification.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 90
stem: What literary term denotes the repetition of initial consonant sounds in neighboring words?
explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant sound at the start of adjacent words.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 91
stem: Identify the device in: 'I have told you a million times to sit down.'
explanation: Hyperbole is an intentional and dramatic exaggeration not meant to be taken literally.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 92
stem: What figure of speech uses pleasant or mild phrasing to mask a harsh reality?
explanation: A euphemism substitutes a mild or indirect term for one considered harsh or blunt (e.g. 'passed away').

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 93
stem: Identify the literary device in: 'The classroom was an absolute silence deafened by whispers.'
explanation: An oxymoron brings together two contradictory terms in a single phrase.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 94
stem: What poetic device reproduces the sound of the object it depicts (e.g., 'buzz', 'hiss')?
explanation: Onomatopoeia words phonetically imitate or resemble the sound that they describe.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 95
stem: What is the central message or underlying moral meaning of a literary text called?
explanation: The theme represents the fundamental idea, moral, or philosophical inquiry explored in a story.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 96
stem: The physical location and time period in which a story unfolds is termed the:
explanation: The setting establishes the geographical, temporal, and historical backdrop of a narrative.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 97
stem: The turning point of greatest emotional intensity in a dramatic plot is the:
explanation: The climax represents the structural peak of dramatic action and decisive conflict resolution.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 98
stem: A character who directly opposes and creates obstacles for the protagonist is the:
explanation: The antagonist stands in opposition to the protagonist, driving narrative tension.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 99
stem: A poem of fourteen lines structured in iambic pentameter is universally known as a:
explanation: A sonnet is a fixed-form lyric poem consisting of fourteen metrical lines.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA English Language Curriculum - Literary Devices Item 100
stem: A mournful, reflective poem composed specifically to lament someone's death is an:
explanation: An elegy is a song or poem written in meditative grief for someone who has died.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Fractions Obj 1
WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Standard Form Obj 2
stem: Express 0.000348 in standard scientific form.
explanation: Move the decimal 4 places to the right: 3.48 × 10⁻⁴.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Number Bases Obj 3
stem: Convert 45 in base ten to a binary numeral (base two).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - HCF & LCM Obj 4
stem: Find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 36, 54, and 90.
explanation: Prime factors: 36=2²×3², 54=2×3³, 90=2×3²×5. Common prime factors with lowest powers: 2¹×3² = 18.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - HCF & LCM Obj 5
stem: Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of 12, 18, and 30.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Indices Obj 6
stem: Simplify: (2³ × 3⁴) ÷ (2 × 3²).
explanation: Apply index laws: 2³⁻¹ × 3⁴⁻² = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Proportion Obj 7
stem: If 5 men weed a farm in 12 days, how many days will 6 men take working at the same rate?
explanation: Inverse variation: total man-days = 5 × 12 = 60. For 6 men: 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Ratio Obj 8
stem: Share GH₵ 7,200 between Kofi and Ama in the ratio 5 : 4. How much does Ama receive?
explanation: Total ratio parts = 5 + 4 = 9. Ama's share = (4/9) × 7200 = 4 × 800 = GH₵ 3,200.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Commercial Arithmetic Obj 9
stem: A trader buys a bag of rice for GH₵ 600 and sells it for GH₵ 750. Calculate the percentage profit.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Commercial Arithmetic Obj 10
stem: Calculate the simple interest on GH₵ 8,000 invested at 15% per annum for 3 years.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Percentages Obj 11
stem: Express 35% as a fraction in its lowest terms.
explanation: 35% = 35/100. Divide numerator and denominator by 5: 7/20.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Decimals Obj 12
stem: Evaluate: 2.4 × 0.05.
explanation: 24 × 5 = 120. Total decimal digits = 1 + 2 = 3. Hence 0.120 = 0.12.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Approximation Obj 13
stem: Round 48,765 to the nearest hundred.
explanation: Tens digit is 6 (≥5), so round the hundreds digit 7 up to 8: 48,800.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Square Roots Obj 14
stem: Evaluate the square root of 0.0144.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Percentages Obj 15
stem: If 15% of a certain number is 45, what is the number?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Fractions Obj 16
stem: Arrange in ascending order: 2/3, 5/8, 3/4.
explanation: Express with common denominator 24: 5/8 = 15/24, 2/3 = 16/24, 3/4 = 18/24. Ascending: 5/8, 2/3, 3/4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Number Bases Obj 17
stem: Solve for n in the base equation: 110₂ + n₂ = 1001₂.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Number Theory Obj 18
stem: Find the difference between the square of 13 and the square of 12.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Indices Obj 19
stem: What is the value of 5⁰ + 5⁻¹ + 5⁻²?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Set Theory Obj 20
stem: If universal set U has 50 elements, n(A)=28, n(B)=22, and n(A ∩ B)=8, find n(A ∪ B)'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebra Obj 21
stem: Solve for x: 4(x - 3) = 2x + 10.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebra Obj 22
stem: Factorize completely: 6a²b - 9ab².
explanation: The HCF of 6a²b and 9ab² is 3ab. Factor out 3ab: 3ab(2a - 3b).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Quadratic Equations Obj 23
stem: Factorize the quadratic expression: x² - 5x + 6.
explanation: Find two numbers whose product is 6 and sum is -5: -2 and -3. (x - 2)(x - 3).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Quadratic Equations Obj 24
stem: Solve the quadratic equation: x² - 9x + 20 = 0.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Simultaneous Equations Obj 25
stem: If 3x + 2y = 12 and x - y = 4, find the value of x.
explanation: From 2nd equation: y = x - 4. Substitute into 1st: 3x + 2(x - 4) = 12 => 5x - 8 = 12 => 5x = 20 => x = 4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Inequalities Obj 26
stem: Solve the linear inequality: 3(x + 2) ≥ 5x - 4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Change of Subject Obj 27
stem: Make 'r' the subject of the formula: V = πr²h.
explanation: Divide by πh: r² = V / (πh). Take square root: r = √(V / (πh)).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebra Obj 28
stem: Expand and simplify: (2x - 3)(x + 4).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Indices Obj 29
stem: Find the value of x if 2^(3x - 1) = 32.
explanation: 32 = 2⁵. Equating indices: 3x - 1 = 5 => 3x = 6 => x = 2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Variation Obj 30
stem: If y varies directly as x and y = 18 when x = 6, find y when x = 10.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebra Obj 31
stem: Solve the equation: (2x + 1)/3 = (x - 2)/2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebra Obj 32
stem: Factorize the difference of two squares: 16x² - 49y².
explanation: a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b) with a=4x and b=7y.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Functions Obj 33
stem: If f(x) = 2x² - 3x + 5, evaluate f(-2).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Logarithms Obj 34
stem: Solve for x: log₂ (x + 6) = 5.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Quadratic Equations Obj 35
stem: Find the roots of the equation: 2x² - 8 = 0.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Algebraic Fractions Obj 36
stem: Simplify: (x² - 4)/(x + 2).
explanation: Numerator is (x - 2)(x + 2). Cancel (x + 2): x - 2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Coordinate Geometry Obj 37
stem: Find the gradient of the straight line 3x + 4y = 12.
explanation: Express in y = mx + c: 4y = -3x + 12 => y = (-3/4)x + 3. Gradient m = -3/4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Coordinate Geometry Obj 38
stem: Find the equation of a line passing through the origin with slope 5.
explanation: Using y = mx + c with m = 5 and c = 0 gives y = 5x.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Inequalities Obj 39
stem: Solve: 5 - 2x < 11.
explanation: -2x < 6. Dividing by -2 reverses the inequality sign: x > -3.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Word Problems Obj 40
stem: The sum of three consecutive integers is 72. Find the smallest integer.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Change of Subject Obj 41
stem: If 1/x + 1/y = 1/z, express z in terms of x and y.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Quadratic Theory Obj 42
stem: Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation 2x² - 4x + 1 = 0.
explanation: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = (-4)² - 4(2)(1) = 16 - 8 = 8.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Logarithms Obj 43
stem: Evaluate log₁₀ (25) + log₁₀ (4).
explanation: log₁₀(25 × 4) = log₁₀(100) = 2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Indices Obj 44
stem: Simplify: (3a³b²)³.
explanation: 3³ × a³ˣ³ × b²ˣ³ = 27a⁹b⁶.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Coordinate Geometry Obj 45
stem: Find the coordinates of the midpoint between P(2, -4) and Q(6, 8).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 46
stem: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 47
stem: Find the perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 14 cm subtending an angle of 90° at the centre.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 48
stem: Calculate the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Take π = 22/7).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Polygons Obj 49
stem: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: Exterior angle = 180° - 140° = 40°. Number of sides n = 360° / 40° = 9.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Pythagoras Theorem Obj 50
stem: Find the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with sides 9 cm and 12 cm.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Trigonometry Obj 51
stem: If tan θ = 4/3 and θ is acute, find the value of sin θ.
explanation: Opposite = 4, Adjacent = 3. Hypotenuse = √(4² + 3²) = 5. sin θ = Opposite/Hypotenuse = 4/5.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Trigonometry Obj 52
stem: A ladder 10 m long leans against a vertical wall making an angle of 60° with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 53
stem: Calculate the total surface area of a closed cube of side 5 cm.
explanation: A cube has 6 congruent square faces: 6 × 5² = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Coordinate Geometry Obj 54
stem: Find the distance between the points A(1, 2) and B(4, 6).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Angles Obj 55
stem: Two angles are complementary. If one angle is 38°, find the other angle.
explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°. Other angle = 90° - 38° = 52°.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Angles Obj 56
stem: Two angles are supplementary. If one angle is 115°, what is the measure of the other angle?
explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180°. Other angle = 180° - 115° = 65°.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 57
stem: Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm, and vertical height 6 cm.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Circle Theorems Obj 58
stem: In a circle, an angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is always:
explanation: Thales's theorem: the angle in a semicircle subtended by a diameter is 90°.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Circle Theorems Obj 59
stem: The angle at the centre of a circle is 80°. What is the angle subtended by the same arc at the circumference?
explanation: The angle subtended at the centre is twice the angle subtended at the circumference: 80° / 2 = 40°.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Polygons Obj 60
stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon (6-sided polygon).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 61
stem: Calculate the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm. (Leave in terms of π).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Bearings Obj 62
stem: A bearing of 225° can be written in compass bearing notation as:
explanation: 225° is in the third quadrant: 225° - 180° = 45° West of South, i.e., S 45° W.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Triangles Obj 63
stem: In triangle ABC, angle A = 65° and angle B = 45°. Find the measure of angle C.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 64
stem: Find the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side length 8.5 cm.
explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides: 3 × 8.5 = 25.5 cm.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Trigonometry Obj 65
stem: If cos θ = 1/2 for an acute angle θ, what is the value of θ?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Pythagoras Theorem Obj 66
stem: Calculate the length of the diagonal of a square with side length 6 cm.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 67
stem: What is the total curved surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm? (Take π = 22/7).
explanation: Curved surface area = πrl = (22/7) × 7 × 25 = 550 cm².

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Mensuration Obj 68
stem: Find the area of an isosceles right-angled triangle with equal legs of length 10 cm.
explanation: Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 10 × 10 = 50 cm².

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Triangles Obj 69
stem: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is 40°. What is the measure of each base angle?
explanation: Base angles are equal: (180° - 40°) / 2 = 140° / 2 = 70°.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Trigonometry Obj 70
stem: The angle of depression of a boat from the top of a cliff 50 m high is 30°. Find the horizontal distance to the boat.
explanation: tan(30°) = opposite/adjacent => 1/√3 = 50 / d => d = 50√3 m.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Vectors Obj 71
stem: What is the magnitude of the vector u = (6, -8)?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Vectors Obj 72
stem: Find the sum of the vectors a = (3, 5) and b = (-1, 2).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Transformations Obj 73
stem: If point P(3, 4) is reflected in the x-axis, what are the coordinates of its image?
explanation: Reflection in the x-axis keeps the x-coordinate unchanged and negates y: (3, -4).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Transformations Obj 74
stem: If point Q(-2, 5) is reflected in the y-axis, what are the coordinates of its image?
explanation: Reflection in the y-axis negates x and preserves y: (2, 5).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Transformations Obj 75
stem: Under a translation by vector T = (4, -3), point A(1, 2) is mapped to:

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 76
stem: Find the mean of the numbers: 6, 8, 12, 14, 20.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 77
stem: Find the median of the set: 15, 7, 22, 13, 9, 18, 11.
explanation: Arrange in order: 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18, 22. The 4th middle value is 13.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 78
stem: Find the mode of the distribution: 4, 7, 9, 7, 3, 7, 4, 8.
explanation: The number 7 appears most frequently (3 times).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 79
stem: Find the range of the test scores: 42, 68, 89, 54, 73, 95, 31.
explanation: Range = Maximum - Minimum = 95 - 31 = 64.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 80
stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of obtaining a prime number?
explanation: Prime outcomes on a die are {2, 3, 5} (3 favorable outcomes out of 6): 3/6 = 1/2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 81
stem: A bag contains 5 red balls, 4 blue balls, and 3 green balls. A ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is blue.
explanation: Total balls = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12. P(Blue) = 4/12 = 1/3.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 82
stem: Two fair coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
explanation: Outcomes: {HH, HT, TH, TT} (4 equally likely outcomes). At least one head: {HH, HT, TH} = 3/4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 83
stem: In a class of 40 students, 24 are girls. What is the probability of selecting a boy at random?
explanation: Number of boys = 40 - 24 = 16. P(Boy) = 16/40 = 2/5.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 84
stem: Find the mean of the first five prime numbers.
explanation: First 5 primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Sum = 28. Mean = 28 / 5 = 5.6.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 85
stem: If the mean of 4, 8, x, 14, and 16 is 11, find x.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Pie Charts Obj 86
stem: In a pie chart, an expenditure of GH₵ 300 out of a total budget of GH₵ 1,200 is represented by an angle of:

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 87
stem: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability of drawing an Ace?
explanation: There are 4 Aces in 52 cards: P(Ace) = 4/52 = 1/13.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 88
stem: What is the median of the even numbers between 5 and 19?
explanation: Even numbers: 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 (7 values). The middle term is 12.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 89
stem: If P(A) = 0.35, what is the probability of the complement of A, P(A')?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 90
stem: The scores of 6 students in a test are 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 11. Find the interquartile range (IQR).
explanation: Lower half: 5, 7, 8 => Q1 = 7. Upper half: 8, 9, 11 => Q3 = 9. IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 9 - 7 = 2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 91
stem: A letter is chosen at random from the word 'MATHEMATICS'. What is the probability that it is a vowel?
explanation: Letters in MATHEMATICS = 11. Vowels are A, E, A, I (4 vowels). P(Vowel) = 4/11.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 92
stem: Find the modal class of the frequency distribution: 1-5 (freq 4), 6-10 (freq 9), 11-15 (freq 14), 16-20 (freq 8).
explanation: The modal class is the interval with the highest frequency (14), which is 11 - 15.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 93
stem: What is the probability of picking an odd number from the integers 1 to 20 inclusive?
explanation: There are 10 odd numbers out of 20: 10/20 = 1/2.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 94
stem: A number is chosen at random from {1, 2, 3, ..., 30}. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 5?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 95
stem: The mean age of 4 boys is 12 years. When a fifth boy joins, the mean age becomes 13 years. How old is the fifth boy?
explanation: Initial total age = 4 × 12 = 48. New total age = 5 × 13 = 65. Fifth boy's age = 65 - 48 = 17 years.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Pie Charts Obj 96
stem: A sector of a pie chart representing agriculture has an angle of 108°. What percentage of the whole activity is agriculture?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 97
stem: Two fair dice are rolled together. What is the probability of rolling a sum of 7?

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Statistics Obj 98
stem: Find the variance of the numbers 2, 4, 6.
explanation: Mean = 4. Deviations squared: (2-4)²=4, (4-4)²=0, (6-4)²=4. Variance = (4+0+4)/3 = 8/3 ≈ 2.67.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 99
stem: If events A and B are mutually exclusive, then P(A ∩ B) is equal to:
explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur simultaneously, so their intersection is the empty set: P(A ∩ B) = 0.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Mathematics Syllabus - Probability Obj 100
stem: A container has 6 black pens and 4 red pens. If two pens are drawn without replacement, find the probability that both are black.
explanation: First draw: 6/10. Second draw: 5/9. P(Both Black) = (6/10) × (5/9) = 30/90 = 1/3.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Reproduction Obj 1
stem: Which part of the flower receives pollen grains during pollination?
explanation: The stigma is the sticky terminal receptive surface of the female carpel that catches pollen.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Cell Biology Obj 2
stem: Which organelle is universally known as the powerhouse of the living cell?
explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP cellular energy through aerobic respiration.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Human Biology Obj 3
stem: Which blood cells are primarily responsible for defending the human body against infectious pathogens?
explanation: White blood cells ingest bacteria and synthesize antibodies to protect the body against infection.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Circulatory System Obj 4
stem: What is the primary function of hemoglobin present in red blood cells?
explanation: Hemoglobin binds reversibly with oxygen in the lungs to form oxyhemoglobin, transporting it throughout the body.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Digestive System Obj 5
stem: Which human organ secretes bile to aid in the emulsification of dietary fats?
explanation: The liver synthesizes bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and emulsifies lipids in the duodenum.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Digestive System Obj 6
stem: Where in the human digestive system does the absorption of most digested nutrients occur?
explanation: The ileum has millions of microscopic villi that absorb amino acids, glucose, and fatty acids into the bloodstream.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Circulatory System Obj 7
stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart?
explanation: The pulmonary vein is the unique vein that carries freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Excretory System Obj 8
stem: What is the basic functional filtering unit of the human kidney?
explanation: Each kidney contains approximately one million nephrons responsible for filtering metabolic wastes from blood.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Biology Obj 9
stem: Which green plant pigment is essential for absorbing radiant solar energy during photosynthesis?
explanation: Chlorophyll inside chloroplasts captures sunlight energy to convert water and carbon dioxide into glucose.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Endocrine System Obj 10
stem: Which hormone regulates blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake into body cells?
explanation: Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas secrete insulin to lower blood glucose levels.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Skeletal System Obj 11
stem: What type of joint permits movement in only one plane, such as the human elbow and knee?
explanation: Hinge joints restrict articulation to back-and-forth movement along a single axis.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Nutrition Obj 12
stem: Which mineral element is indispensable for the healthy development of strong bones and teeth in humans?
explanation: Calcium phosphate provides structural rigidity and mineral density to skeletal bones and tooth enamel.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Nutrition Obj 13
stem: A severe dietary deficiency of Vitamin C results in which nutritional disorder?
explanation: Scurvy is characterized by bleeding gums, skin hemorrhages, and impaired wound healing due to lack of Vitamin C.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Respiratory System Obj 14
stem: Which respiratory structures in the mammalian lungs are the actual sites of gaseous exchange?
explanation: Alveoli are thin-walled, moist, highly vascularized air sacs where oxygen diffuses into blood and carbon dioxide exits.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Physiology Obj 15
stem: What process describes the loss of water vapor from the aerial parts of plants through stomata?
explanation: Transpiration is the evaporative loss of water vapor predominantly via stomatal pores in plant leaves.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Genetics Obj 16
stem: In genetics, what is the observable physical expression or characteristic of an organism called?
explanation: The phenotype is the detectable outward anatomical, biochemical, or behavioral trait resulting from gene expression.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Genetics Obj 17
stem: How many chromosomes are present in a normal, unfertilized human gamete (ovum or sperm)?
explanation: Gametes are haploid cells produced by meiosis and possess 23 chromosomes (half the somatic diploid count).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Diseases Obj 18
stem: Which vector transmits the plasmodium parasite responsible for malaria in humans?
explanation: The female Anopheles mosquito requires a blood meal to mature her eggs and vectors the Plasmodium protozoan.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Microbiology Obj 19
stem: Which microorganism is utilized in baking to cause dough to rise through anaerobic fermentation?
explanation: Yeast ferments sugars anaerobically, liberating carbon dioxide gas bubbles that expand the bread dough.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Digestive System Obj 20
stem: What is the muscular involuntary contraction that propels boluses of food along the alimentary canal?
explanation: Peristalsis involves alternating radial and longitudinal smooth muscle contractions pushing food downwards.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Nervous System Obj 21
stem: Which part of the human brain coordinates muscular balance, posture, and voluntary motor coordination?
explanation: The cerebellum integrates sensory inputs from the inner ear and muscles to maintain equilibrium and coordination.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Biology Obj 22
stem: What is the protective outer covering of a seed that shields the embryo from mechanical injury?
explanation: The testa is the tough integumentary outer coat that prevents desiccation and bacterial invasion.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Digestive System Obj 23
stem: Which enzyme present in human saliva commences the chemical digestion of cooked starch into maltose?
explanation: Ptyalin breaks down complex amylose starch chains into simpler disaccharide maltose in the mouth.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Genetics Obj 24
stem: A condition in which the blood fails to clot normally due to lack of specific clotting factors is:
explanation: Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive genetic disorder causing delayed or defective blood coagulation.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Ecology Obj 25
stem: What is the symbiotic relationship where both cooperating species derive mutual nutritional benefit?
explanation: Mutualism is an ecological association where both participating organisms benefit mutually (e.g. nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legumes).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Inorganic Chemistry Obj 26
stem: What is the chemical formula for common table salt?
explanation: Common table salt is sodium chloride, composed of sodium and chlorine ions in a 1:1 lattice.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Acids and Bases Obj 27
stem: What is the pH value of pure distilled neutral water at standard room temperature (25°C)?
explanation: A pH of 7 represents a neutral solution with equal concentrations of hydronium and hydroxide ions.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Gases Obj 28
stem: Which gas turns clear limewater (calcium hydroxide solution) milky or turbid?
explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with limewater to form an insoluble white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Periodic Table Obj 29
stem: What is the atomic number of carbon, which determines its position as group 14 in the periodic table?
explanation: Carbon possesses 6 protons in its atomic nucleus, giving it an atomic number of 6.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Atomic Structure Obj 30
stem: Which subatomic particle carries a negative electrical charge and orbits outside the atomic nucleus?
explanation: Electrons carry a unit negative charge (-1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) and occupy quantized energy shells.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Separation Techniques Obj 31
stem: What separation technique is most suitable for separating two miscible liquids with different boiling points?
explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids based on differences in their respective boiling points.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - States of Matter Obj 32
stem: What change of state occurs when a solid changes directly into a gas without melting into a liquid?
explanation: Sublimation is the direct phase transition from solid to gaseous state (e.g. iodine, solid CO₂, camphor).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Thermochemistry Obj 33
stem: Which chemical reaction releases thermal energy into the surrounding environment, raising the temperature?
explanation: Exothermic processes liberate net heat energy into their surroundings during bond formation.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Acids and Bases Obj 34
stem: What color does blue litmus paper turn when dipped into an acidic solution such as dilute hydrochloric acid?
explanation: Acidic solutions turn moist blue litmus paper distinctly red.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Atmospheric Chemistry Obj 35
stem: Which element is the most abundant gas by volume in the Earth's lower atmosphere?
explanation: Molecular nitrogen (N₂) comprises roughly 78.08% of dry atmospheric air by volume.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Chemical Bonding Obj 36
stem: What type of chemical bonding involves the mutual sharing of electron pairs between non-metallic atoms?
explanation: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms achieve noble gas octets through shared electron pairs.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Chemical Bonding Obj 37
stem: What type of bond is formed by the complete electrostatic transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal?
explanation: Ionic bonds arise from electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged cations and anions.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Industrial Chemistry Obj 38
stem: What is the chemical name and formula for quicklime?
explanation: Quicklime is manufactured by thermally decomposing limestone to yield calcium oxide (CaO).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Metals Obj 39
stem: Which process describes the slow chemical oxidation of iron in the presence of atmospheric oxygen and moisture?
explanation: Rusting produces hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O) requiring both oxygen and water.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Elements Obj 40
stem: Which metal is liquid at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure?
explanation: Mercury has a melting point of -38.8°C, remaining liquid under ambient conditions.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Elements Obj 41
stem: What is the universal chemical symbol for gold?
explanation: The symbol 'Au' derives from the Latin name for gold, 'Aurum'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Elements Obj 42
stem: What is the universal chemical symbol for silver?
explanation: Silver takes its symbol 'Ag' from its Latin designation, 'Argentum'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Elements Obj 43
stem: What is the universal chemical symbol for lead?
explanation: Lead derives its chemical symbol 'Pb' from the Latin root 'Plumbum'.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Acids and Bases Obj 44
stem: What is formed when an acid reacts completely with a chemical base in a neutralization reaction?
explanation: Acid + Base → Salt + Water (H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Carbon Chemistry Obj 45
stem: Which non-metal is an allotrope of carbon capable of conducting electric current efficiently?
explanation: Graphite possesses delocalized electrons in hexagonal layers that move freely under an electric field.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Minerals Obj 46
stem: What is the hardest naturally occurring mineral substance on Mohs hardness scale?
explanation: Diamond exhibits a rigid 3D tetrahedral network covalent lattice giving it maximum hardness (10).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Solutions Obj 47
stem: What happens to the solubility of most solid solutes in liquid water when the temperature is elevated?
explanation: Thermal energy facilitates the endothermic dissociation of solid solute lattices into solvent cages.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Gases Obj 48
stem: Which laboratory gas burns with a characteristic squeaky 'pop' sound when a glowing splint is introduced?
explanation: Hydrogen mixes with atmospheric oxygen to burn with an explosive micro-combustion pop sound.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Gases Obj 49
stem: Which gas relights or rekindles a glowing wooden splint placed inside its test tube?
explanation: Oxygen supports combustion vigorously, causing a glowing ember on a splint to burst into flame.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Organic Chemistry Obj 50
stem: What is the common name for dilute aqueous ethanoic acid (acetic acid) used in food preservation?
explanation: Vinegar is a 4-8% dilute solution of ethanoic acid widely utilized in domestic pickling and seasoning.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Heat Energy Obj 51
stem: Which form of heat transfer travels effectively through empty vacuum space without needing matter?
explanation: Radiation propagates through space via transverse electromagnetic waves without requiring a material medium.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Mechanics Obj 52
stem: What is the standard International System (SI) unit of force?
explanation: The newton (N) is defined as the force required to accelerate 1 kilogram of mass at 1 m/s².

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Electricity Obj 53
stem: What is the standard SI unit of electrical potential difference (voltage)?
explanation: The volt (V) measures electric potential difference and electromotive force.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Electricity Obj 54
stem: What is the standard SI unit of electric current?
explanation: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge measured in amperes (A).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Energy Obj 55
stem: What is the standard SI unit of energy and mechanical work done?
explanation: The joule (J) is the work done when a force of 1 newton acts through a displacement of 1 meter.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Energy Obj 56
stem: What is the standard SI unit of power, representing work done per unit time?
explanation: The watt (W) represents the rate of energy transfer equivalent to one joule per second.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Simple Machines Obj 57
stem: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
explanation: In a second class lever, the load is situated between the fulcrum (the wheel) and the applied effort (handles).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Simple Machines Obj 58
stem: A pair of scissors or a crowbar represents which class of lever?
explanation: In a first class lever, the fulcrum is located between the effort and the load.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Simple Machines Obj 59
stem: What is the mechanical advantage (MA) of a simple machine that moves a 600 N load with an effort of 150 N?
explanation: MA = Load / Effort = 600 N / 150 N = 4.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Energy Transformations Obj 60
stem: What energy transformation occurs in an electric bulb connected to an active dry cell battery?
explanation: Chemical energy in battery electrolytes yields electrical current, converted into radiant light and heat.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Optics Obj 61
stem: What is the speed of light in a vacuum, rounded to standard scientific approximation?
explanation: Light propagates in a vacuum at exactly c ≈ 299,792,458 m/s, conventionally written as 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Optics Obj 62
stem: The bending of light rays as they pass obliquely from one optical medium into another of different density is:
explanation: Refraction occurs due to changes in wave speed when light enters an optical medium of differing refractive index.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Optics Obj 63
stem: What optical lens is thicker in the middle than at its edges and converges parallel incident light rays?
explanation: Convex lenses converge parallel incident light rays onto a real focal point behind the lens.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Optics Obj 64
stem: Which visual defect in humans prevents distant objects from being focused sharply on the retina?
explanation: In myopia, light rays from distant objects converge in front of the retina; it is corrected using concave lenses.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Optics Obj 65
stem: What visual defect is corrected by wearing spectacles fitted with converging (convex) lenses?
explanation: Hypermetropia occurs when images focus behind the retina, corrected by converging convex lenses.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Electricity Obj 66
stem: According to Ohm's Law, what is the mathematical relationship between Voltage (V), Current (I), and Resistance (R)?
explanation: Ohm's law dictates that current is directly proportional to voltage: V = IR.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Electricity Obj 67
stem: What electrical safety device contains a thin wire that melts to break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit?
explanation: A fuse breaks the electrical path by resistive thermal melting to protect wiring from hazardous overcurrent.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Sound Waves Obj 68
stem: Which property of sound waves determines its perceived pitch (how high or low it sounds)?
explanation: Pitch is governed directly by frequency (number of sound wave oscillations per second in Hertz).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Sound Waves Obj 69
stem: Which property of a sound wave determines its loudness and acoustic intensity?
explanation: Loudness depends on wave amplitude; greater amplitude corresponds to greater acoustic pressure and energy.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Gravity Obj 70
stem: What is the acceleration due to gravity (g) at the surface of the Earth, conventionally used in physics calculations?
explanation: Earth's standard gravitational acceleration at sea level is approximately 9.81 m/s² (frequently rounded to 10 m/s²).

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Mechanics Obj 71
stem: What is the density of an object with a mass of 400 g and a volume of 50 cm³?
explanation: Density = Mass / Volume = 400 g / 50 cm³ = 8 g/cm³.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Fluids Obj 72
stem: What principle states that an object submerged in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced?
explanation: Archimedes' principle explains buoyant upthrust forces acting on partially or fully immersed bodies.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Instruments Obj 73
stem: What instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
explanation: Barometers measure ambient atmospheric air pressure using mercury columns or aneroid capsules.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Instruments Obj 74
stem: What instrument is used to measure the relative humidity of the atmosphere?
explanation: A hygrometer (such as a psychrometer) measures the quantity of moisture or water vapor in the atmosphere.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Instruments Obj 75
stem: What instrument measures the relative density of liquids such as milk or battery acid?
explanation: A hydrometer floats in liquids to indicate relative density directly on a calibrated stem.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Soil Science Obj 76
stem: Which agricultural soil type has the smallest particle diameter and the greatest water retention capacity?
explanation: Clay particles are microscopic (<0.002 mm), packed closely with tiny micropores that retain water tightly.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Soil Science Obj 77
stem: Which soil type is generally regarded as the most fertile and suitable for cultivating most food crops?
explanation: Loam contains a balanced blend of sand, silt, clay, and decomposed organic humus, ensuring aeration and drainage.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Environmental Issues Obj 78
stem: The illegal small-scale mining in Ghana commonly called 'galamsey' damages water bodies primarily through:
options: Toxic pollution with mercury and heavy siltation
explanation: Galamsey utilizes mercury and heavy alluvial dredging that poisons water basins and destroys aquatic fauna.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Ecology Obj 79
stem: What is the primary greenhouse gas released by human activities that contributes most to global warming?
explanation: Carbon dioxide from fossil fuel combustion traps outgoing infrared terrestrial radiation, causing global warming.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Soil Science Obj 80
stem: Which biological process involves bacteria converting atmospheric nitrogen into soluble nitrates in the soil?
explanation: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen into bioavailable ammonium and nitrates.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Pollution Obj 81
stem: What ecological term describes excessive algal blooms in water bodies caused by runoff of agricultural fertilizers?
explanation: Excess phosphate and nitrate runoff triggers explosive algal blooms that consume dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Agriculture Obj 82
stem: Which primary macronutrient in commercial NPK fertilizers is primarily responsible for vegetative leaf and shoot growth?
explanation: Nitrogen is vital for synthesizing amino acids and chlorophyll, driving vigorous vegetative leaf development.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Agriculture Obj 83
stem: Which nutrient in NPK fertilizers is critical for stimulating root development and fruit/seed formation?
explanation: Phosphorus encourages strong root system development, early seedling vigor, and flower/fruit set.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Soil Conservation Obj 84
stem: What method of soil conservation involves plowing and planting across the slope of a hill rather than up and down?
explanation: Contour plowing creates horizontal ridges that slow down surface runoff and prevent topsoil erosion on hillsides.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Agronomy Obj 85
stem: Which agricultural practice helps break pest and disease cycles by alternating crops of different botanical families?
explanation: Crop rotation deprives species-specific soil pests and weeds of their preferred host plants across successive seasons.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Soil Science Obj 86
stem: What is the dark, nutrient-rich organic component of soil formed by the thorough decomposition of leaves and animal manure?
explanation: Humus is the amorphous organic colloidal substance that enhances soil structure, cation exchange, and water retention.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Atmospheric Science Obj 87
stem: Which atmospheric layer contains the ozone shield that filters harmful solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation?
explanation: The stratospheric ozone layer absorbs destructive solar UV-B and UV-C rays that cause skin cancer and cataract.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Diseases Obj 88
stem: What vector transmits the bacterium Pasteurella pestis, which caused the historical bubonic plague?
explanation: The rat flea acts as the ectoparasitic vector transmitting plague from infected rodent hosts to humans.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Diseases Obj 89
stem: Which fly transmits the microfilarial worms responsible for river blindness (onchocerciasis) in West Africa?
explanation: Simulium blackflies breed in rapidly flowing river rapids and vector Onchocerca volvulus larvae.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Veterinary Science Obj 90
stem: Which disease in cattle is characterized by ulcerating vesicles on the hooves and mouth caused by an aphthovirus?
explanation: Foot-and-mouth is a highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed livestock inducing painful lesions and lameness.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Breeding Obj 91
stem: What is the process of removing male tassels from maize plants to produce hybrid seeds called?
explanation: Detasseling prevents self-pollination in female seed parent rows during the production of commercial hybrid maize.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Agricultural Mechanization Obj 92
stem: What agricultural implement is designed to break up large soil clods and level seedbeds after plowing?
explanation: Harrows pulverize stubborn soil clods, level seedbeds, and uproot emerging weed seedlings.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Crop Protection Obj 93
stem: Which parasitic plant attaches to cocoa tree branches, absorbing moisture and synthesized nutrients from the host?
explanation: Mistletoe is a semi-parasitic vascular plant with haustorial roots that penetrate cocoa branches, reducing tree yield.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Food Preservation Obj 94
stem: What chemical method is used to preserve fresh fish over extended periods by drying and smoke curing in coastal Ghana?
explanation: Traditional smoking dehydrates fish flesh and deposits antimicrobial phenolic smoke compounds, preventing spoilage.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Hematology Obj 95
stem: What component of blood initiates clot formation by adhering together at the site of a laceration?
explanation: Platelets aggregate at endothelial tears and release thromboplastin to trigger the clotting cascade.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Excretion Obj 96
stem: Which human body organ detoxifies chemical drugs and converts toxic ammonia into less harmful urea?
explanation: The liver performs deamination of excess amino acids and converts ammonia via the ornithine cycle into urea.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Taxonomy Obj 97
stem: What is the term for animals that possess a vertebral column or backbone?
explanation: Vertebrates belong to phylum Chordata and are defined by possessing an axial vertebral column.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Zoology Obj 98
stem: Which warm-blooded vertebrate class feeds its offspring with milk produced by maternal mammary glands?
explanation: Mammalia are distinguished by hair/fur, endothermy, three middle ear ossicles, and functional mammary glands.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Plant Anatomy Obj 99
stem: What is the primary function of stomatal guard cells in the epidermis of plant leaves?
options: Regulating the opening and closing of stomata for gas exchange and transpiration
explanation: Turgor pressure changes in bean-shaped guard cells control the stomatal pore aperture.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Integrated Science Syllabus - Energy & Environment Obj 100
stem: Why is renewable energy such as solar, wind, and hydro preferred over fossil fuels for sustainable national development?
options: It is inexhaustible and produces little or no greenhouse gas emissions
It is unavailable in tropical countries
explanation: Renewable resources replenish naturally and generate clean energy without depleting finite carbon reserves.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environment of Ghana Q1
stem: What is the highest mountain peak in Ghana?
explanation: Mount Afadja (Afadjato) in the Volta Region is the highest mountain peak in Ghana with an elevation of about 885 meters.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environment of Ghana Q2
stem: Which water body forms the southern natural boundary of Ghana?
explanation: Ghana is bounded on the south by the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Physical Features Q3
stem: What is the largest artificial lake in the world by surface area, located in Ghana?
explanation: Lake Volta covers approximately 8,502 square kilometers and is the world's largest artificial reservoir by surface area.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Physical Features Q4
stem: Which natural meteorite impact lake is situated in the Ashanti Region of Ghana?
explanation: Lake Bosomtwe is a natural lake situated in an ancient meteorite impact crater in Ashanti Region.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Climate and Weather Q5
stem: The prevailing wind that brings dry, dusty conditions across Ghana between November and February is the:
explanation: The Northeast Trade Winds blow from the Sahara Desert across West Africa bringing dry, dusty Harmattan conditions.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Vegetation Zones Q6
stem: Which climatic zone in Ghana is characterized by high rainfall and equatorial evergreen forest?
explanation: The southwestern corner around Ankasa and Axim experiences the highest rainfall and wet evergreen rainforest.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environmental Degradation Q7
stem: What is the primary cause of desertification in the northern ecological zones of Ghana?
explanation: Overgrazing, tree cutting for fuelwood, and annual bush burning severely deplete vegetative cover leading to desertification.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Resource Conservation Q8
stem: The process of restoring trees and forest cover to degraded land in Ghana is known as:
explanation: Reforestation involves replanting trees on deforested or cleared landscapes.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Natural Resources Q9
stem: Which major mineral resource is famously mined at Obuasi in the Ashanti Region?
explanation: Obuasi is renowned globally for having one of the richest and oldest underground gold mines.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Energy and Resources Q10
stem: At which coastal town in the Western Region of Ghana was crude oil first struck in commercial quantities in 2007?
explanation: Commercial petroleum was discovered offshore Cape Three Points in the Jubilee Field in 2007.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Natural Resources Q11
stem: Which mineral is extensively mined at Nsuta near Tarkwa?
explanation: Nsuta in the Western Region is the primary center for manganese mining in Ghana.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Natural Resources Q12
stem: Bauxite deposits in Ghana are predominantly mined at which location?
options: Awaso in the Western North Region
explanation: Awaso hosts the major operational commercial bauxite mine in Ghana.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Natural Resources Q13
stem: Which Ghanaian town is historically famous for alluvial diamond mining along the Birim River?
explanation: Akwatia in the Eastern Region is the primary center of diamond production in Ghana.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environmental Challenges Q14
stem: What environmental menace is locally termed 'galamsey' in Ghana?
explanation: Galamsey refers to illegal, unregulated artisanal small-scale mining that severely pollutes rivers and destroys farm lands.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Water Bodies and Pollution Q15
stem: Which Ghanaian river has suffered severe pollution and turbidity due to illegal alluvial mining?
explanation: River Pra, along with Birim and Offin, has experienced drastic siltation and heavy metal pollution from galamsey.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environmental Conservation Q16
stem: What is the term for the wearing away of topsoil by flowing water and intense wind?
explanation: Soil erosion is the detachment and removal of topsoil by erosive agents such as torrential rain and strong wind.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Wildlife and Habitat Q17
stem: The Ramsar convention sites along Ghana's coast, such as Songor and Keta, are designated to protect:
explanation: Ramsar sites protect internationally recognized wetland habitats and nesting grounds for waterfowl.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Tourism and Conservation Q18
stem: Which National Park in the Savannah Region of Ghana is the country's largest wildlife sanctuary?
explanation: Mole National Park covers about 4,840 square kilometers and is Ghana's largest wildlife reserve.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Eco-Tourism Q19
stem: Kakum National Park in the Central Region of Ghana is famous for which unique eco-tourism feature?
explanation: Kakum is world-renowned for its canopy walkway suspended high above the tropical rainforest floor.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Environmental Policy Q20
stem: Which agency of government in Ghana is legally mandated to protect and regulate the environment?
explanation: The EPA is the statutory body responsible for regulating, monitoring, and enforcing environmental protection standards.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - National Independence Q21
stem: On which date did Ghana achieve political independence from British colonial rule?
explanation: Ghana became an independent sovereign dominion on 6th March 1957 under Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Constitutional History Q22
stem: When did Ghana become an independent Republic with its first President?
explanation: On 1st July 1960, Ghana promulgated its first republican constitution and Dr. Kwame Nkrumah was sworn in as President.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Colonial Treaties Q23
stem: Who was the British governor that signed the historic Bond of 1844 with Fante chiefs?
explanation: Lieutenant Governor Henry Worsley Hill signed the Bond of 1844 on behalf of the British Crown.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Anti-Colonial Struggle Q24
stem: The 1948 Christiansborg Crossroads shooting incident led to the death of which prominent Ghanaian ex-serviceman?
explanation: Sergeant Adjetey, along with Corporal Attipoe and Private Odartey Lamptey, was shot dead while marching peacefully to Christianborg Castle.

syllabusRef: WAEC / NaCCA Social Studies Syllabus - Nationalist Movements Q25
stem: Who were the 'Big Six' leaders arrested by the colonial authorities following the 1948 riots?
options: Nkrumah, Danquah, Akufo-Addo, Ako-Adjei, Obetsebi-Lamptey, and Ofori Atta I
Nkrumah, Busia, Limann, Rawlings, Kufuor, and Mills
Grant, Casely Hayford, Mensah Sarbah, Guggisberg, Maclean, and Hill
Aggrey, Yaa Asantewaa, Prempeh, Osei Tutu, Komfo Anokye, and Naa Gbewaa
